newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn still wants to sell all of Lufthansa.
newsitem.headline: Bonn still wants to sell all of Lufthansa.

text.p: The German government is still planning to sell all of its remaining holdings in carrier Deutsche Lufthansa AG, a senior Finance Ministry official said on Thursday.
"We want to get out of Lufthansa completely, all the way down to zero," Eberhard Rolle, head of the ministry's department for government holdings, told Reuters.
The German government currently holds around 36 percent of Lufthansa and has said it would like to complete the privatisation of the airline by the end of 1997.

Rolle said the government welcomed the decision by the European Commission to allow the sale of further shares in Lufthansa but that it must now study the conditions placed on Bonn before deciding how and when to sell its shares.
The government is busy with preparations for the partial privatisation of telecommunications giant Deutsche Telekom AG, which will sell nearly 25 percent of its capital to the public next week.
Rolle said the government will not begin making firm plans for a further sale of Lufthansa until after the Telekom sale.
"It is unlikely to happen this year, Christmas is just a month away. But we will begin making preparations next week, after Telekom," he said.
He added that it was not clear what conditions or restrictions would be placed on Bonn's sale of Lufthansa shares by the Commission.

"We have to study the document first. We are not certain yet how this will be done technically, whether we can sell it all at once or in parts. But our goal remains the same, to get out of Lufthansa completely," he said.
